title: Pitch link to pitch plate -- the grip-length joint as a topology

joint.description: The 5-place joint in DETAIL B: NAS6403U11D bolt down through the pitch-link eye (spherical bearing) and a plain bushing, through a 4.06 mm pitch-plate lug, retained by a slotted nut + cotter pin over a flat washer.
joint.scope: Grip length only, and only along the bolt axis. Out of scope, deliberately: diameter and hole fits; bushing-to-bore interference; the pitch link's own internal stack; the joint at the other end of the pitch link; torque and preload.

provenance.values: NONE are copied. Every edge carries a `dimension_ref` into the stack file above, resolved at load time by tolerance_stack.topology.load_topology, so this document cannot drift away from the numbers that stack publishes. Every value's citation and confidence is whatever that element already carries -- this topology adds no source_ref of its own to any value and closes no gap the stack has open.
provenance.structure: The nodes and the edge orientation are a READING of the stack's element order and roles, not a sourced claim, exactly as topology_vpa_output_to_pitch_plate.json's structure note describes for the L1 proof. The stack's own notes give the axial order from the bolt head: bushing, [pitch-link eye -- MISSING], pitch-plate lug, washer; this topology reads that order literally and does NOT insert an interface for the missing pitch-link eye -- there is no element to hang one on, and inventing a placeholder node/edge for an unsourced member would be exactly the kind of invention the repo's one rule forbids. The bolt's own fastener dimensions (grip, overall length, cotter-hole-to-point) are read as edges sharing additional interfaces beyond the clamped stack's own (the bolt's point, and the cotter-hole centreline), which is what turns this graph into more than L1's single grounded loop: the clamped-stack/grip loop (closing at the derived `shank_out` gap) and the length/grip/thread-region loop (closing at the derived `thread_region` edge), which share the bolt-head interface.
provenance.part_identity: The bolt (NAS6403U11D), the pitch-plate lug (215197) and the washer (NAS1149V0332H) are named on the stack's own citations. The plain bushing (214820-002) is likewise named by the stack's parts-list citation. No part identity is invented here that the referenced stack does not already claim.

parts.name: NAS6403U11D bolt, .1900-32, .688 grip
parts.note: Balloon 5X in DETAIL B, per the referenced stack's parts list. A standard part; its dimensional identity is the NAS6403-NAS6420 Rev 4 sheet the referenced elements cite.

parts.name: 214820-002 BUSHING, PLAIN, ALUMINUM BRONZE, .1900 in ID X .1875 in LONG
parts.note: Balloon 8X in DETAIL B per the referenced element's source_ref. The Joby part drawing for 214820-002 is not in this repo -- see the referenced element's own gap note.

parts.name: pitch plate (215197), 5X 4.06 +/-0.10 flange group
parts.note: The referenced element's source_ref names this drawing and zone D10, the 5X group distinct from the 3X (tangential link) and 1X (VPA output) groups on the same sheet.

parts.name: NAS1149V0332H washer, flat, 6Al-4V, .203 x .438 x .032 in
parts.note: Balloon 8X in DETAIL B per the referenced element's source_ref (find 32, qty 9 across the assembly).

nodes.name: bolt-head bearing face against the plain bushing
nodes.note: Where the grip is measured from: NAS6403-NAS6420 Rev 4 sheet 2 note (a) defines grip as underside of head to the end of the full cylindrical shank, per the referenced fastener elements' source_ref.

nodes.name: plain bushing face toward the pitch-plate lug
nodes.note: A reading, not a claim of physical adjacency: the stack's own notes place the pitch-link eye / spherical bearing between the bushing and the pitch-plate lug, and that member is UNSOURCED (no document in this repo gives it). This interface reproduces the stack's own arithmetic, which simply omits the missing member from the sum -- it does not assert the bushing and the lug actually touch. See the two checks' `excluded_terms` for the same omission, stated the stack's way.

nodes.name: pitch-plate lug face against the flat washer
flat washer far face -- the last modelled clamped surface
nodes.note: A datum_feature and not a mate: beyond it sits the slotted nut (MS9363-09) and cotter pin (MS24665-153), deliberately outside this joint's scope, exactly as topology_vpa_output_to_pitch_plate.json's bushing_far_face is.

nodes.name: end of the bolt's full cylindrical shank
nodes.note: The grip's far end, defined by NAS6403-NAS6420 Rev 4 sheet 2 note (a). Not a mate: it is where the thread run-out begins.

nodes.name: bolt point (tip)
nodes.note: The far end of `bolt_length_11` (head bearing face to point) and the near end of `cotter_hole_from_point` (cotter-hole centreline to bolt point).

nodes.name: cotter-pin hole centreline
nodes.note: NAS6403-NAS6420 Rev 4 sheet 1, dimension M, read off the figure per the referenced element's own source_ref note.

edges.name: fastener grip, NAS6403U11D (.688 in)
edges.note: Runs PARALLEL to the clamped stack rather than in series with it. Together with `shank_out` it closes the loop `study_pitch_link_shank_out.json` sums.

edges.name: NAS6403U11D overall length, head bearing face to point (1.011 in)
edges.note: Runs PARALLEL to `fastener_grip` + `thread_region` (together they close the loop `study_pitch_link_thread_region_t.json` sums) and to `cotter_hole_from_point` reversed (together with the clamped stack, the loop `study_pitch_link_cotter_hole_clearance.json` sums).

edges.name: cotter-hole centreline to bolt point (dimension M)
shank out -- full-diameter shank beyond the modelled clamped stack
edges.note: A DERIVED gap: it carries no dimension because it is the quantity `study_pitch_link_shank_out.json` computes. Its endpoints share no part (the washer, the bolt), so it is kind `gap` rather than a structural dimension. This is check `shank_out__11_sourced_only`'s own residual, and per that check's own guidance the missing pitch-link eye is what would need to fill it.

edges.name: thread run-out and point region beyond the full-diameter shank
edges.note: A DERIVED edge -- carries no dimension. Both its interfaces are on the bolt, so it is `structural` (kind `gap` is only for interfaces sharing no part), but it is `derived` in the same sense `shank_out` is: nothing in this repo sources this sub-region directly. `study_pitch_link_thread_region_t.json` computes it as `bolt_length_11 - fastener_grip`, reproducing the referenced stack's `thread_region_T` path exactly -- the stack's own notes call that quantity 'a provenance cross-check, not a design quantity', since it happens to equal NAS6403's T (Ref).

notes: This document adds no value, no citation and no confidence claim of its own. If a number here looks wrong, the stack file docs/tolerance_stacks/stack_pitch_link_to_pitch_plate.json is where it is wrong.

The graph: 4 parts, 7 interfaces, 8 edges, 3 branch points, 2 grounded loops (the clamped-stack/grip loop, and the length/grip/thread-region loop), 1 gap edge (`shank_out`; `thread_region` is derived but structural, since both its ends are on the bolt).

The pitch-link eye / spherical bearing -- the joint's own MISSING member -- is not modelled as a node or an edge, exactly as the stack's own checks record it in `excluded_terms`. This topology does not invent an interface for it.

OPEN, for a future reviewer, exactly as topology_vpa_output_to_pitch_plate.json flags the same kind of question: this topology asserts an axial order for the clamped members (bushing, pitch-plate lug, washer, head-side first) taken from the stack's own element order and notes. The sum does not depend on it -- a chain sum is invariant to ordering -- but a reader looking at the rail diagram will read it as physical.
